pids.019A: hybrid/EV vehicle system data, battery, voltage

source: obd-discover, on-car captures 2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30; VIN pattern read from the vehicle. Signal names cross-referenced against OBDb's Hyundai-IONIQ-5 signalset, cited per entry.
notes:
Battery electric, and that is why its VIN was hard to read: a BEV has no engine ECU, so 7E0 does not exist on this car and every VIN attempt before discovery went to an address that is not there. vPIC confirms make, model, year and SE trim independently of the WMI mapping.

EVERY IDENTIFIER HERE ANSWERED ON THE 7DF BROADCAST. Five headers are live -- 744, 7DF, 7E2, 7E3, 7E4 -- but recon finished only four of them and no block was ever attributed to a physical header, so the physical addresses remain unswept. That matters for the 14 cross-referenced signals below: OBDb documents all of them at 7E4, 7E5 or 7E2, and this car answered every one of them on the broadcast. The battery dataset was obtained without ever sweeping the battery module.

OBDb DOCUMENTS 11 REQUESTS THIS PROJECT HAS NOT FOUND, and nine sit on headers it does not probe by design -- 7C6 (odometer, 22B002), 7A0 (tire pressures), 730 (wheel speeds, steering angle, yaw), 7B3 (cabin temperatures), 770 (exterior lights). A scope decision rather than a scanning failure.

AND 120 IDENTIFIERS HERE ARE IN NO PUBLISHED LIST. Roughly 43 of those are structural -- 22F1xx is ISO 14229's identification range and 22F4xx mirrors the legislated Mode-01 PIDs -- leaving about 77 genuine unknowns. The most tractable are 220106, 220107, 220108 and 220130: neighbours in the same battery block whose surrounding entries OBDb has already decoded.

SCANNING HISTORY. On 2026-08-30 this vehicle stopped recognising either of its keys after a session that drew 5,740 refusals in ten minutes. It recovered unaided overnight. See docs/pacing.md -- including what that evidence is not.
